title: Add benchmark-lab mixed-workload runners, profiling baselines, and reporting pipeline
author: Priya Nair
description: Adds a new end-to-end mixed-workload runner for the benchmark-lab, a set of updated profiling baselines for realistic latency/throughput distributions, and a reporting pipeline that aggregates and publishes per-run metrics to the telemetry store. Motivation: recent customer workloads showed mixed inference patterns (short chat turns interleaved with long generation tasks) that weren't well represented by existing runners; profiling baselines were stale and produced noisy regression signals; and reporting was fragmented across jobs. This PR introduces: 1) mixed_workload_runner: a configurable runner that simulates realistic session-level mixes, support for workload profiles in YAML, warmup phase handling, and KV-cache recycling behavior. 2) profiling/baselines/v2: new baseline traces and JSON summaries for p95/p99 latency, token throughput, and memory footprints across representative models and sequence-length buckets. 3) pipelines/reporting_pipeline_v72.yaml: a modular Dagster pipeline that ingests runner outputs, normalizes metrics, computes regression deltas against baselines, and writes summary artifacts to telemetry (and S3). 4) CI: a benchmark job to run a scaled-down mixed workload on PRs and post results to the PR comment. 5) docs: README updates describing runner configs and guidance for adding new profiles. Checklist: - [x] mixed workload runner implemented and unit-tested (- small simulation harness) - [x] profiling baseline generation scripts added - [x] reporting pipeline and CI job added - [x] docs updated - [x] perf smoke-tests passing Notes and caveats: the baseline set deliberately chooses conservative thresholds to avoid noisy alerts; follow-up PR planned to add automatic baseline rolling and per-customer tagging. Related: ENG-4729 and ENG-4801.
